summary.text: A woman in her 70s with a history of gastric cancer treated by total abdominal gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y reconstruction presented to the emergency department with sudden epigastric pain that began during the night. She was admitted and antibiotic treatment was started. On admission the abdomen was flat and soft with localized tenderness, and blood tests showed an elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein.

Contrast-enhanced CT on admission showed edematous wall thickening of the duodenum. The patient continued to have a fever and the inflammatory response did not improve on cefmetazole, so plain CT was repeated and revealed a duodenal diverticulum stone with increased surrounding fatty tissue, allowing the diagnosis of duodenal diverticulitis associated with a parapapillary stone.

Endoscopic stone removal was attempted on day 9 with a small-bowel double-balloon endoscope. The stone, lodged in the diverticulum with a white purulent discharge, was crushed with forceps, washed out and removed. A contrast study then showed a fistula from the diverticulum into the blind end of the afferent loop without contrast leakage, and the procedure ended without suture. Fever and inflammation improved rapidly and she was discharged on the 17th day.
